title.narrative: UPSET Holding: validating the market for PurFi textile rejuvenation technology in India

description.narrative: India is the third largest textile producer in the world and therefor has an abundance of post-production waste available for textile recycling. Yet, most material is used for down-cycling as opposed to upcycling, whilst there is an increasing demand from Western Europe and the United States for sustainable textile products from recycled material. In order to upcycle textile and cotton waste in India, high quality and affordable fibres are needed, which currently is a bottleneck. Dutch social venture UPSET Textiles (hereafter: UPSET) has the ambition to realise the production of 100% socially fair and circular yarns in India and considers innovation the only way forward to overcome these bottlenecks, such as lack of infrastructure and technology, for large scale and commercially viable textile recycling. UPSET is in the process of setting up a joint-venture with PurFi (the IP-owner of a ground-breaking rejuvenation technology for cotton) to market PurFi rejuvenation technology in India. Through this, UPSET aims to create a 100% circular and socially fair supply chain around the rejuvenation technology through innovative service-models for waste holders and textile producers.To prepare for future investments in India, Technical Assistance (DGGF-TA) provided support to validate the market. The project included an assessment of customer demand for upcycled fibres, a feasibility study into the set-up of a rejuvenation facility, an assessment of the supply chain, partner identification and validation of the technology and supported 6 direct jobs over the course of the project. The validation was successful and further investments in the set-up of a local sorting centre and production facility are currently being prepared. This facility is likely to create 275 high skilled jobs and will contribute to innovation and sustainability within the textiles supply chain.
